subject: Hiring tranche plan & risk mitigation ahead of QBR
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Hiring tranche plan & risk mitigation ahead of QBR

Team —

Ahead of next week’s QBR I pulled together a proposed tranche approach to prioritize hires and reduce near-term cash exposure. The goal is to give leadership a simple decision to: (1) greenlight a short list of mission-critical reqs now, (2) defer lower-impact reqs into conditional tranches, and (3) identify mitigations (contractors, reprior) for the remainder.

Attached: hiring_tranche_matrix.xlsx and qbr_headcount_summary.pdf (also on Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c_hiring_matrix)

High-level proposal:
- Tranche A (Approve now): 2 FTEs — RQ-1184 (Infra Reliability Engineer), RQ-1199 (Inference Runtime SWE). These are flagged as high delivery risk if delayed.
- Tranche B (Post-QBR conditional): 3 roles (1 PM, 2 SWE) — proceed to offer contingent on QBR budget approval / convert contractors where feasible.
- Tranche C (Freeze): all non-critical growth roles and exploration hires for next quarter (list in attachment).

Mitigations suggested:
- Temporarily increase contractor coverage for customer-facing support (ContractorOps looped)
- Shift two senior ICs from lower-priority projects for 6–8 weeks to cover key milestones
- Reduce open req pipeline activity for non-critical roles to avoid needless spend

Requests: please review the matrix and flag any blockers by EOD Tuesday 6/1. If we have consensus I’ll prepare a condensed approval package for the QBR deck and a DocuSign for the two Tranche A reqs so recruiting can start immediately.

Key ask: sign-off or major objections by 2027-06-02 COB.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Planning & Strategy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: hiring_tranche_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: qbr_headcount_summary.pdf (summary PDF)]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hiring tranche plan & risk mitigation ahead of QBR

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A few quick questions before I can endorse Tranche A:
1) Cash sensitivity: what is the incremental monthly run-rate for the two Tranche A hires (salary + benefits ramp)? Please include on-target hiring cost and expected ramp schedule.
2) Contingency: if QBR budget does not clear Tranche B, what is our fallback timeline to convert contractors?
3) Deal/Customer impact: any external contracts (e.g., AcmeHealth) that depend on hiring timing? If so we should highlight that in the CFO package.

I attached a short note with the sensitivity model I ran — see cash_sensitivity_note.pdf. If the delta is material I’ll want to push one of the hires into a delayed start (30–45d) rather than immediate.

Markus Klein
SVP, Finance & Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: cash_sensitivity_note.pdf (analysis)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hiring tranche plan & risk mitigation ahead of QBR

On Tue, May 30, 2027 at 09:14 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> Ahead of next week’s QBR I pulled together a proposed tranche approach...

I reviewed the matrix — thanks for synthesizing. A couple of product-side notes:
- RQ-1184 (Infra Reliability) is mission critical. We had three incidents last quarter where we’ll need that capacity to finish the KV-cache stabilization work; delaying this one adds measurable SLO risk.
- For RQ-1199 (Inference Runtime SWE), if finance needs a buffer we can negotiate a 30–45 day start date with the candidate (they’re amenable). That would preserve the hire and reduce immediate cash pressure.
- For Tranche B’s PM spot, I recommend we prioritize the candidate with domain infra experience — otherwise cost of delay for the infra roadmap increases.

Operational asks:
- Vanessa: can you create a consolidated recruiter brief and put the two Tranche A reqs into expedited sourcing if we get sign-off?
- Karthik: please add a short slide to QBR deck that ties hires to near-term SLO and customer commitments (AcmeHealth is mentioned in the contract appendix).

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T14:52:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hiring tranche plan & risk mitigation ahead of QBR — consolidated decision

Folks —

Thanks for the feedback. Consolidating decisions for QBR package and recruiting:
- APPROVE Tranche A (start recruiting immediately): RQ-1184 and RQ-1199. Vanessa please open expedited reqs and instruct TA to begin offers.
- TRANCHE A START DATES: RQ-1184 start immediate; RQ-1199 start can be delayed 30–45 days if finance requests a buffer (per Laura).
- CONDITIONAL Tranche B: advance offers contingent on QBR budget. If budget not approved, we convert 2 of the 3 roles from contractors (ContractorOps) within 60 days.
- FREEZE Tranche C until next quarter.

Next actions: 
1) Vanessa: consolidate recruiter briefs and candidate scorecards by EOD Monday 6/7.
2) Markus: accepted — I saw your cash sensitivity note. I’ll fold a one-slide summary into the CFO packet highlighting the incremental run-rate (will call out salary+onboard cost).
3) Approvals: I created a DocuSign packet for the two Tranche A req approvals to speed recruiting — link: https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abc123. Please sign by COB 6/03 if you agree.

I’m marking this as leadership-level decision for the QBR deck. If anyone has an objection raise it by 6/03 COB and I’ll escalate to the exec committee.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Planning & Strategy
Redwood Inference
